newsitem.title: USA: Distinctive Clinton college postcard sells.
newsitem.headline: Distinctive Clinton college postcard sells.

text.p: A collector of presidential memorabilia paid $4,125 for a postcard illustrated with a racially charged picture that President Bill Clinton sent 30 years ago to his grandmother.

The postcard, dated in 1966, made clear the future president did not pick out the card and there were no racist comments in his writing. Herman Darvick of Rockville Centre, New York, who auctioned off the postcard, said on Friday it was the picture that made the postcard distinctive.

The picture of a smiling black boy polishing a 195-pound (88 kg) watermelon was accompanied by an inscription that identified Clinton's hometown of Hope, Arkansas, as "Home of the World's Largest Watermelon."

In the postcard the 19-year-old Georgetown University student wrote to his grandmother in an Arkansas nursing home, "Dear Mammaw, Thought I would send you one of your cards just to prove I'm using them!"
The picture of the child with the watermelon evoked a racist image projected at the time of black people in the South as being poor and uneducated.

But the auctioneer said in defence of Clinton, "He didn't pick them out, it's not that detrimental, it won't lose him the black vote or anything. It's something that he sent out in 1966 that he wouldn't send out in 1996."
Clinton, who also wrote "My tests are over and I'm just starting the second term," signed it "Bill" and scribbled above his return address "Wm. J. Clinton".

Darvick sold the postcard Thursday night to a Los Angeles collector who asked not to be identified. He previously sold a love letter written to a girlfriend by Clinton when he was a student at Oxford University in England.
